sources.title: RE2 regular-expression library
sources.sections_read: Dated release announcement and engine description
sources.confirmed: The 2010 announcement describes an open-source C++ regular-expression engine using automata, bounded stack space, and a BSD-style license.
sources.limits: A Rust wrapper needs an FFI boundary and native build support; the live header documents a restricted pattern dialect and is not a verified 2010 snapshot. sources.title: Boost.Xpressive static and dynamic regular expressions
sources.version_or_date: Boost 1.37.0; release date verified separately as 2008-11-03
sources.sections_read: Introduction, static/dynamic expressions, examples, and header-only installation
sources.confirmed: Xpressive supports runtime strings and compile-time expression templates, including mixing them; its static syntax is constrained by C++ syntax.
sources.limits: C++ expression templates are a design precedent, not directly reusable Rust code; host-language syntax changes the pattern notation and static expansion adds compilation work. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: pre_decision. Original read and any failures remain in runs/A/C17.json.

sources.title: Rust regex crate 1.0.0
sources.version_or_date: regex 1.0.0; release date verified separately as 2018-05-01
sources.sections_read: Crate introduction, raw-string examples, reuse with lazy_static, captures, replacement, and Unicode
sources.confirmed: The Rust library supplies compilation and search APIs, UTF-8 matching, captures, and cached initialization; it omits look-around and backreferences.
sources.limits: This version is later than the cutoff; cached lazy initialization avoids repeated runtime compilation but does not itself compile patterns during the Rust build. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: post_decision. Original read and any failures remain in runs/A/C17.json.

sources.title: PCRE saved compiled patterns
sources.sections_read: Saving and reusing compiled patterns; compatibility; revision, also inspected with find
sources.confirmed: Compiled patterns can be saved and restored, subject to byte order, character tables, and version compatibility; JIT data cannot be serialized.
sources.limits: Serialization depends on engine versions, byte order, and character tables; JIT data cannot be saved, and Rust integration adds FFI/build maintenance. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: pre_decision. Original read and any failures remain in runs/A/C17.json.

sources.confirmed: Current re2c converts expressions into generated lexer code and lists Rust among its targets. The site links a 1994 paper, but that paper could not be opened.
sources.limits: Lexer behavior needs adaptation for general substring search and captures; current Rust backend availability was not established before the cutoff. sources.title: Lua 5.1 standard string patterns

sources.limits: Lua pattern syntax differs from conventional regex syntax, and its byte/locale assumptions would require explicit redesign for Rust UTF-8 text.
